title: Painted tin-can herb planters
title_ar: أصص أعشاب من علب الصفيح المطلية
summary: Food cans with drainage holes and painted outsides make a matching row of herb planters for a sunny sill.
summary_ar: علب طعام بثقوب تصريف وطلاء خارجي تصنع صفًا متناسقًا من أصص الأعشاب لنافذة مشمسة.
result: three steel food cans with labels removed, painted in matte pastel colors on the outside, planted with basil, mint and parsley
steps_outline: Soak off the labels and wash the cans
Rub the rim with sandpaper so no sharp burr is left
Stand each can upside down on wood and punch 3-4 drainage holes with a hammer and nail
Paint the outside only and let it dry fully
Add stones, soil and a herb seedling
safety: Wear work gloves: can rims and punched holes are sharp
Wear a dust mask while sanding the rim and wipe the metal dust away with a damp cloth
Paint the outside only and keep the soil side bare

title: Punched tin-can lantern
summary: A pattern of nail holes punched into a can throws dots of light across the wall when a tea light glows inside.
summary_ar: نقش من ثقوب المسمار في علبة الصفيح يرسم نقاط ضوء على الجدار عندما تتوهج شمعة صغيرة بداخلها.
result: a steel can with a pattern of small punched holes forming a star, a wire handle on top and warm candlelight shining through the holes
steps_outline: Fill the clean can with water and freeze it overnight so it holds its shape
Tape a paper pattern around the can
Lay it on a towel and punch along the pattern with a hammer and nail
Punch two holes near the rim and fit a wire handle with pliers
Let the ice melt, dry the can and add a tea light
safety: Wear work gloves and safety glasses while punching
Metal gets hot around a flame: lift it by the handle only and never leave it unattended

title: Rope-wrapped can caddy
title_ar: حامل أقلام من علب ملفوفة بالحبل
items: aluminium cans with the top removed
summary: Cans wrapped in twine or rope and glued together make a desk caddy for pens, brushes and scissors.
summary_ar: علب ملفوفة بخيط القنّب أو الحبل وملصوقة معًا تصنع حاملًا مكتبيًا للأقلام والفرش والمقصات.
result: three steel cans of different heights tightly wrapped in natural jute rope and glued side by side, holding pens and scissors
steps_outline: Wash the cans and cover each rim with a strip of masking tape
Glue the end of the rope at the base of a can
Wind the rope up in tight rows, gluing every few turns
Glue the finished cans together in a cluster
Fill with pens and brushes
safety: Tape or file the rims first: opened cans have sharp edges

title: Jar-lid photo magnets
summary: Metal jar lids framing small photos or patterned paper become fridge magnets and gifts.
summary_ar: أغطية البرطمانات المعدنية تؤطر صورًا صغيرة أو أوراقًا منقوشة لتصبح مغناطيسات للثلاجة وهدايا.
result: four round metal jar lids used as frames, each holding a small family photo, stuck to a white fridge door
steps_outline: Wash and dry the lids
Trace the inside of a lid on the photo and cut the circle
Glue the photo inside the lid
Glue a magnet to the back and let it cure
safety: Keep magnets away from small children who could swallow them

title: Can and lid wind chime
summary: Cans and lids hung at different lengths from a stick ring softly against each other in the breeze.
summary_ar: علب وأغطية معلقة بأطوال مختلفة من عصا ترنّ بهدوء عندما يلامس بعضها بعضًا مع النسيم.
result: a driftwood stick with four small painted tin cans and several jar lids hanging from twine at different lengths, moving in the breeze
steps_outline: Wash the cans and lids and tape or file any sharp rims
Punch a hole in the centre of each can base and lid with a hammer and nail on a board
Thread twine through each hole and knot a bead or washer inside to stop it
Tie the strings along the stick at different lengths
Add a twine loop to hang it and adjust until the pieces touch
safety: Wear work gloves and safety glasses when punching metal

title: Wall-mounted can organizer
summary: Cans screwed to a board by their sides hold brushes, tools or utensils on a workshop or kitchen wall.
summary_ar: علب مثبتة بالبراغي على لوح من جوانبها تحمل الفرش أو الأدوات على حائط الورشة أو المطبخ.
result: a painted wooden board on a wall with five steel cans screwed on in a staggered pattern, holding brushes, pliers and screwdrivers
steps_outline: Sand the board and plan where each can will sit
Drill a small hole in the side of each can near the rim and near the base
Screw the cans to the board through the holes, with a washer under each screw
Tape or file the can rims
Fix the board to the wall and fill the cans
safety: Wear safety glasses when drilling, a dust mask when sanding the board and work gloves when handling cans
Clamp or hold cans with a cloth while drilling: the bit can grab thin metal

title: Embossed can plant markers
title_ar: علامات نباتات منقوشة من علب الألمنيوم
summary: Flat aluminium cut from a drink can takes embossed letters with a pen, making weatherproof plant labels.
summary_ar: ألمنيوم مسطح مقطوع من علبة مشروب يُنقش عليه بالقلم ليصنع علامات نباتات تتحمل الطقس.
result: several shiny aluminium plant markers with rounded corners and embossed herb names, pushed into pots of basil and mint
extra_materials: a folded towel to press on
steps_outline: Rinse the can and let it dry
Pierce the side with the craft knife, then cut off the top and bottom with scissors
Cut the sheet into strips and round every corner with scissors
Lay each strip on a towel and write the plant name firmly with a ballpoint pen
Push the markers into the soil or tape them to sticks
safety: Wear work gloves the whole time: cut aluminium edges are very sharp
Round every corner and fold back any burr

title: Jar-lid coasters
summary: Wide metal lids lined with felt or cork from an old board make a set of sturdy drink coasters.
summary_ar: أغطية معدنية واسعة مبطنة باللباد أو الفلين من لوح قديم تصنع طقمًا متينًا من قواعد الأكواب.
result: four round metal jar lids turned upside down, each filled with a snug disc of grey felt, a glass of water standing on one
extra_materials: felt, cork or thick fabric scraps
steps_outline: Wash the lids and remove any rubber seal that is loose
Trace a lid on felt or cork and cut a disc slightly inside the line
Glue the disc into the lid and press it flat
Glue a small felt circle underneath so it doesn't scratch tables
safety: Let the glue cure for a day before putting wet glasses on them
